headline: Your Smartphone Feels Your Invisible Touch
source: IEEE Spectrum, How Capacitive Touchscreens Work; MIT Technology Review, The Science Behind Touchscreens

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Invisible Touch? 🖐️
slides.bubble: Did you know your phone feels your finger without *actually* touching it? That's wild!

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: It's True! ✨
slides.bubble: Yes! Your screen has an invisible electric field. Your body disrupts it when you get close.

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Electric Field? ⚡
slides.bubble: Wait, so it's not sensing physical pressure, like old tech? How does that even work?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Electric Pond 🌊
slides.bubble: Imagine the screen's surface is a still electric pond. Your finger is a pebble creating ripples.

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Before I Touch? 😲
slides.bubble: So, it 'sees' the ripple and knows I'm there, even before my skin hits the glass?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Invisible Sensation 🪄
slides.bubble: Exactly! It's sensing your electrical presence, not just physical contact. Pure invisible magic!

takeaway: Your smartphone doesn't just react to pressure. It senses your body's electrical field, detecting your touch before physical contact. It's invisible tech at work!
caption:
🧠 DID YOU KNOW? 🤯

Your smartphone's screen can 'feel' your finger *before* you even touch it! Here's the mind-blowing reality:

*   📱 **Invisible Electric Field:** Your screen is covered by an invisible electrical force field.
*   ✋ **You Create Ripples:** Your finger, being electrically conductive, subtly disrupts this field when it gets close.
*   ✨ **Instant Detection:** The screen detects these tiny electrical changes, pinpointing your 'touch' instantly.
